question.problem: Which of the following describes the level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}?$
question.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \frac{1}{3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} & =c \\ c(3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =1 \\ 3c{x}^{2}+c{y}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $f(x,y,z)$ can't be zero or negative. Therefore, we get a family of surfaces given by

$$
3c{x}^{2}+c{y}^{2}=1,\,c\in (0,\infty ).
$$

choices.value: A family of surfaces given by $3c{x}^{2}+c{y}^{2}=1$
A family of surfaces given by $3c{x}^{2}-c{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$
A family of surfaces given by $3c{x}^{2}-c{y}^{2}=1$
A family of hyperboloids of one sheet: $3c{x}^{2}+c{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}=1$

responses.value: A family of surfaces given by $3c{x}^{2}+c{y}^{2}=1$
